[QUERENT] the compression frontier

[ANSWER]

The phrase "compression frontier" appears across a few key contexts in artificial intelligence, engineering, and research:
1. The Attribution–Compression Frontier in RAG
In AI research, The Attribution–Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (a paper by Deepanshu Mody accepted to the GroundLM workshop at EMNLP 2026) investigates what happens to source citations and attribution when you shrink or compress retrieved documents before feeding them to a language model. [1, 2]

* Key Finding: While compressed text or summaries can look well-supported internally (high precision against the summary itself), their actual traceability back to original source passages drops significantly. For example, on the ASQA dataset, a RECOMP-style compressor scored 86% citation precision against its own summary, but only 12% against the underlying source text. [1, 2]

2. Strategy and Summarizer Layers
Writers and strategists (such as Lee Sharks in The Compression Frontier) use the term to model how information moves through answer pipelines and AI search layers. [1]

* Ungoverned Compression: Summarizes and discards structure without preserving clear provenance or a visible account of what was lost. [1]
* Governed Compression: Maintains traceability and makes discarded structure legible to the user or system. [1]

3. Frontier Model Performance Compression
In industry evaluations (such as the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index), the frontier model index has compressed tightly. The top flagship AI models (such as Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet variants) now sit within a razor-thin 2-point margin of one another, shifting competitive advantage away from raw benchmark scores and toward pricing, speed, and ecosystem integration. [1]
4. Technical Compressor Optimization
In industrial and hardware contexts, the "compression frontier" also refers to real-time AI and machine-learning models optimizing physical gas compressors and machinery pipelines (such as AI-driven gas station optimization increasing production within OEM limits) or KV-cache compression on hardware architectures like Apple Silicon. [1, 2]
Which of these contexts are you looking to explore? I can break down:

* The RAG attribution and loss paper details
* Model KV-cache or algorithmic compression
* AI benchmarking and pricing moats
